metadata.title: Wrenfield | Ballard
metadata.description: Wool goods woven on the Ottauquechee since 1919.

props.description: Wool goods woven on the Ottauquechee since 1919. Blankets, heavy shirts, and a coat for standing still in the cold.

paragraphs: The mill sits in a brick building on the river, and it has for a hundred and six years. Eleven looms, four of them older than anyone who works there. The wool comes from Vermont and New York farms, the same farms for decades, and it's spun on site.

Wrenfield became part of Ballard in 2025. The mill kept its name, its people, and its way of doing things, which is slower than Ballard's and suits the wool. What changed is that you can bring a Wrenfield blanket into any Ballard store for rebinding, and the Mill Shirt is in a few of them.
The goods are heavy, they want a cold room, and moths like them. That's honest, and so is the rest: a Wrenfield blanket will outlast the bed it's on.

items.heading: Care
items.description: Dry clean or hand wash cold. Never a dryer. Store in cedar over summer.

items.heading: Repair
items.description: Blankets are rebound and shirts get new buttons and elbows at the mill. Any Ballard store will send it for you.

items.heading: Visit
items.description: The mill store is open Thursday through Sunday, 10 to 4. 2140 Route 4, Bridgewater, VT.
